rationale: It runs automated license and copyright scanners from the command line and emits SPDX, giving a concrete way to auto-collect license information from source material.

Its deduplication and one-click SPDX/notice generation reconcile license and copyright findings aggregated across an entire distribution, supporting accurate license tracking when combining many sources.
It automatically lists licenses found in images, directories and SBOMs, providing an automated license-collection step.
Its policy engine categorizes and checks licenses across all components aggregated in an SBOM, letting you audit license correctness when materials come from many sources.
It automates license and copyright detection over repositories with low-noise results, directly implementing scalable license collection.

It resolves and attributes dependencies from many manifests/lockfiles into complete SBOMs with package URLs, reconciling license/provenance data aggregated from multiple sources with an emphasis on accuracy.
It automatically analyzes project components to detect and report restricted/uncompliant licenses on every code update, implementing automated license collection and compliance checking.
It provides a fast, module-based automated method for identifying problematic data (PII, secrets, weak crypto) across whole repositories, a building block for scanning large corpora.
Its scan/redact/replace/hash operations remove or mask PII from text and datasets, directly implementing removal of problematic data.
The optional Spark/distributed profile (SparkService, PII UDFs) applies its detection engine across large distributed datasets, addressing how identification scales.
Its pkg/redact and stdin gateway redact detected sensitive values in place (simple, format-preserving, or synthetic strategies), implementing removal of harmful data from files and streams.
It masks detected PII in place across data formats and database dumps via configurable masking strategies, implementing removal of sensitive data from datasets.
It identifies PII columns and then drops or encodes them to emit a new de-identified dataset plus a mapping log, implementing removal of problematic data from a dataset.
It redacts detected PII from text (placeholder, mask, token-replace, format-preserving modes) to keep sensitive data out of logs and pipelines, implementing removal of problematic data.
It orchestrates automated detection and image-level redaction of sensitive quotes from PDFs at scale, implementing removal of problematic data from a document corpus.
Using OCR word-level bounding boxes it automatically redacts detected PII from images in batch, implementing removal of sensitive data from image datasets.
It removes redacted content irretrievably rather than merely covering it, directly implementing removal of harmful data in a way that does not leave the data recoverable.

It creates cryptographically verifiable provenance manifests and links between datasets and their sources, providing a tamper-evident way to attest and verify source metadata (including license/provenance claims) when aggregating datasets from multiple sources.
It reconstructs a dataset's origins and shared upstream sources purely from public metadata (dataset cards, repos, papers) without needing direct access to the dataset contents.
By surfacing shared sources and benchmark-related nodes in the lineage graph it reveals contamination risk between datasets, helping detect problematic overlap/contamination.
It regenerates benchmark problems at evaluation time and provides DyPass@K specifically to give contamination-resistant, faithful assessment of models when training-data contamination is suspected.

It detects and redacts/anonymizes sensitive text and visual regions across unstructured files in batch and exports the cleaned artifacts, implementing removal of problematic data from document/image datasets.
